model: Galaxy Digital is a crypto financial-services firm whose trading, lending, asset management and staking businesses, together with its own crypto and venture holdings, drive reported earnings and make them swing with digital asset prices. It is also a data center landlord. At its Helios campus in West Texas (1.63 GW of approved grid power), Galaxy leases 526 MW of critical IT capacity to a single tenant, CoreWeave, under near-triple-net 15-year leases with 3-5% escalators: 133 MW has been paying rent since 2Q26 (about $80mn a quarter), 260 MW is due from 2Q27 and 133 MW in 2028. Each phase is financed through its own project subsidiary with secured debt (a $1.4bn Deutsche Bank loan for Phase I; $3.5bn of 9.875% notes due 2031 for Phase II), so returns depend on yield on cost (about 14-17%) exceeding the cost of that debt, and on CoreWeave paying. The upside is 830 MW of approved but uncontracted Helios power plus about 4 GW of Texas sites awaiting ERCOT approval.
name: Galaxy Digital
